title: A title that appears with a person already in it
question: Which job classes show up in the payroll for the first time with only one or two people in them, who were they, and where had they been the year before?
finding: 184 job classes were paid for the first time after fiscal 2013, the first year of the file. Of those first paid from fiscal 2018 on, when holders can be named, 56 started with one or two holders: 12 went to people who were not on the payroll the year before, 37 were exempt from civil-service hiring and 6 carry a generic title; the number with no rate in either published pay table is 1. The class pages and classification actions date 44 of the 56: 20 were created in the fiscal year they were first paid or the one before, so the class was written and filled together, and 24 were older classes that had stood unused. For the other 12 no creation date is published; 10 of them had a pay rate in the published tables more than a year before anyone was paid in them. In all, 34 of the 56 are older classes.
how: City payroll file. A class is new when nobody was paid in it in any earlier fiscal year back to 2013. The first holders’ earlier job is read from the payroll by name, and only for names that pass the matching rules (one spelling, one person, rare). The rate is a year’s pay at the hourly rate actually paid in the first year. The published-rate column comes from the two pay tables the Department of Human Resources publishes; the older begins in July 2014. Generic titles are listed first, then classes filled from outside the payroll, by rate. The creation date is the origination date printed on the class’s page on the City careers site or, failing that, the fiscal year of a classification action that established it; about half of all class pages print no origination date. Board seats, elected offices and the Superior Court are left out.
limits: A class can first be paid in a year for dull reasons: an old class renumbered (several here are an existing title with the tag SFERS added, and the payroll carries the same titles tagged PERS, which suggests the same job under another number), a merger of two classes, a new apprenticeship step, or a post created by a Charter amendment, as with the Inspector General in the Controller’s office (Proposition C of November 2024, whose text is in the document library). On standing exempt classes: the Charter lists the categories of exempt appointment. The payroll cannot show whether the post was advertised or who asked for it; the classification action and the job announcement would. Someone absent the year before may have worked for the City before 2017, when the file has no names.
